title: European Leagues Chief: 'Infantino Has No Future at FIFA'
detail: Claudius Schaefer, president of European Leagues — a body representing 53 professional men's and women's football leagues — said in an interview with The Athletic published Wednesday that Gianni Infantino cannot continue leading FIFA. 'The influence of the president has grown from year to year' and 'major decisions are taken without meaningful consultation,' Schaefer said, adding institutional reform of the presidency's powers matters more than simply replacing Infantino with someone else. He pointed to two specific episodes as evidence of governance breakdown: FIFA's inaugural Peace Prize awarded to President Trump in December without proper consultation, and the overturning of USMNT forward Folarin Balogun's suspension during the World Cup after Trump personally intervened — which Schaefer called 'a real scandal' that let political interference undermine sporting integrity. Schaefer's comments add a fifth major voice — alongside UEFA, the AFC, CONCACAF, and the six Nordic federations — to the bloc pressuring Infantino as he seeks a fourth term at the March 18, 2027 election in Rabat.

media.caption: Claudius Schaefer (European Leagues) and Gianni Infantino — Schaefer said Aug 26 that Infantino 'has no future' at FIFA

title: Romanian Football Federation Withdraws Support for Infantino's Re-Election
detail: The Romanian Football Federation (FRF) announced Wednesday it would not back Gianni Infantino for a fourth term as FIFA president, citing the fallout from his abandoned World Cup commercial stake-sale plan and his handling of decisions in the tournament's aftermath, including deference to President Trump's public comments about players. FRF president Răzvan Burleanu said the federation had 'lost confidence' in Infantino and that 'this simply means that we will not vote for him if he does not withdraw and run in March 2027.' Romania is among a small minority of federations that had not sent FIFA a letter of support for the 2027 election; more than 200 of FIFA's 211 member associations had reportedly pledged support roughly a month earlier. Romania's withdrawal, alongside Italy's FIGC the same day, added to a growing bloc of European federations breaking with Infantino ahead of the March 18, 2027 vote in Rabat.

media.caption: Gianni Infantino, whose re-election bid lost Romanian Football Federation support on Aug 26

title: Italian Football Federation Withdraws Support for Infantino's FIFA Re-Election Bid
detail: The Italian Football Federation (FIGC) announced Wednesday it would no longer back Gianni Infantino's bid for a fourth term as FIFA president in the March 2027 election, citing 'the recent initiatives promoted by the FIFA president concerning governance and the development of international competitions' — a reference to Infantino's now-abandoned plan to sell a 20% stake in a new World Cup commercial entity. FIGC president Giovanni Malagò said the federation would 'continue to work alongside UEFA and the other European federations to promote a vision of football based on merit, solidarity, sustainability and the central role of fans,' emphasizing 'a model based on dialogue, listening and shared responsibility.' Italy joins England, Germany, the Netherlands, Ireland, New Zealand, Scotland, Israel, Montenegro, North Macedonia, and all six Nordic federations in publicly withdrawing support for Infantino's re-election.

media.caption: FIGC president Giovanni Malagò, who announced Aug 26 that Italy is withdrawing support for Infantino's FIFA re-election bid
